Set scores

singscore (Foroutan et al. 2018) gives every run one score per gene set. Within a run, it ranks all genes by abundance and averages the ranks of the set’s members. A set whose members sit high in that run scores high. The score depends only on ranks inside one run, so it does not move when other runs are added or removed. This step computes scores and describes them; it tests nothing.

Packages

singscore is called with :: where used.

library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)
source(here("00_Setup", "Shared_functions", "analysis_reporting_helpers.R"))

Inputs

Ranking needs every protein in every run and cannot carry a covariate, so the input is limpa’s complete matrix with each protein’s blood slope removed (DAList_corrected.rds). That matrix inherits the blood-removal problem shown in 03_Quantification: the 85 proteins measured in 20 or fewer runs track blood more after removal, not less.

out <- here("01_Processing", "05_Set_Scores", "c_data")
dir.create(out, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
inputs <- c(
  gene_sets = "01_Processing/04_Gene_Sets/c_data/gene_sets.rds",
  proteins = "01_Processing/03_Quantification/c_data/DAList_corrected.rds"
)
paths <- map_chr(inputs, here)
stopifnot(file.exists(paths))
gs <- readRDS(paths[["gene_sets"]])
proteins <- readRDS(paths[["proteins"]])
c(sets = length(gs$sets), proteins = nrow(proteins$data), runs = ncol(proteins$data))
    sets proteins     runs 
    1378     1900       45

Sets are keyed on gene symbols, so the matrix rows switch from accessions to the representative gene chosen in 04_Gene_Sets.

gene_map <- filter(gs$protein_map, selected)
stopifnot(
  identical(gene_map$uniprot_id, intersect(gene_map$uniprot_id, rownames(proteins$data))),
  !anyDuplicated(gene_map$gene)
)
gene_matrix <- as.matrix(proteins$data)[gene_map$uniprot_id, ]
rownames(gene_matrix) <- gene_map$gene
gene_matrix[1:3, 1:3]
         S03_T1   S10_T1   S16_T1
GATD3B 25.72102 25.15538 25.38419
ESYT2  16.25513 16.23097 16.03984
ILVBL  16.32408 16.30989 16.19766

Scores

rankGenes() ranks genes within each run. multiScore() scores every set in one pass and also returns each set’s dispersion: the spread (median absolute deviation) of its members’ ranks within a run. Low dispersion means the members sit together; high means they scatter. By default singscore centres the score so that 0 means the members’ average rank equals the run’s middle rank (package behaviour).

ranks <- singscore::rankGenes(gene_matrix)
scored <- singscore::multiScore(ranks, upSetColc = gs$sets)
scores <- scored$Scores
stopifnot(
  identical(rownames(scores), names(gs$sets)),
  identical(colnames(scores), colnames(proteins$data))
)
dim(scores)
[1] 1378   45
round(scores[1:3, 1:4], 3)
                                      S03_T1 S10_T1 S16_T1 S22_T1
Hallmark|HALLMARK_ADIPOGENESIS         0.170  0.164  0.169  0.155
Hallmark|HALLMARK_ALLOGRAFT_REJECTION -0.013 -0.016  0.001 -0.010
Hallmark|HALLMARK_ANDROGEN_RESPONSE    0.013  0.029  0.017 -0.015

Spread across sets within a run reflects which genes each set holds. Spread across runs within a set is what the trait analyses use. Both are recorded.

score_summary <- tibble(
  n_sets = nrow(scores), n_samples = ncol(scores),
  min = round(min(scores), 4), max = round(max(scores), 4),
  mean = round(mean(scores), 4),
  mean_sd_across_sets = round(mean(apply(scores, 2, sd)), 4),
  mean_sd_across_samples = round(mean(apply(scores, 1, sd)), 4)
)
score_summary
# A tibble: 1 × 7
  n_sets n_samples    min   max   mean mean_sd_across_sets
   <int>     <int>  <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>               <dbl>
1   1378        45 -0.317 0.409 0.0426               0.102
# ℹ 1 more variable: mean_sd_across_samples <dbl>
set_spread <- gs$set_catalog |>
  filter(qualifies) |>
  transmute(set_id, collection) |>
  mutate(
    score = rowMeans(scores[set_id, ]),
    dispersion = rowMeans(scored$Dispersions[set_id, ])
  )
collection_spread <- set_spread |>
  summarise(
    n_sets = n(), median_score = round(median(score), 4),
    median_dispersion = round(median(dispersion), 1), .by = collection
  )
collection_spread

  ggplot(aes(score, group_time)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "grey85", colour = NA) +

How much of the score variation is the person

A PCA of the score matrix, then a one-way ANOVA of PC1 and PC2 on the person (subject). The subject share is the fraction of each component’s variance that person identity explains. A large share is why the trait step analyses within-person change beside the baseline level.

components <- prcomp(t(scores), scale. = FALSE)
variance <- summary(components)$importance[2, 1:4]
targets <- proteins$metadata[match(rownames(components$x), proteins$metadata$sample_id), ]
participant_share <- map_dbl(1:2, function(i) {
  terms <- summary(aov(components$x[, i] ~ targets$subject))[[1]]
  terms[1, 2] / sum(terms[, 2])
})
structure_check <- tibble(
  component = paste0("PC", 1:4),
  variance_explained = round(as.numeric(variance), 3),
  subject_share = c(round(participant_share, 3), NA, NA)
)
structure_check
# A tibble: 4 × 3
  component variance_explained subject_share
  <chr>                  <dbl>         <dbl>
1 PC1                    0.257         0.579
2 PC2                    0.205         0.453
3 PC3                    0.072        NA    
4 PC4                    0.07         NA

Summary

1378 sets were scored in 45 runs. Scores range from -0.32 to 0.41. Person identity explains 58% of PC1 and 45% of PC2.

Save

singscore.rds is read by the set contrasts, classification and trait steps.

saveRDS(list(scores = scores), file.path(out, "singscore.rds"), compress = "xz")
sheets <- list(
  score_summary = score_summary,
  collection_spread = collection_spread,
  set_spread = set_spread,
  structure_check = structure_check,
  set_scores = rownames_to_column(as.data.frame(scores), "set_id")
)
holds <- c(
  "Range and spread of the score matrix.",
  "Median score and dispersion per collection.",
  "Mean score and dispersion per set across samples.",
  "Variance explained by the first four components, and the subject share of PC1 and PC2.",
  "The set by sample score matrix, as saved in singscore.rds."
)
write_workbook(sheets, holds, file.path(out, "set_scores.xlsx"), inputs, paths)
